en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Tenth Chapter
The Discourse on the Two Kinds of Virtue:
Is one who possesses the path endowed with two kinds of virtue?
Yes, he is.

Is one who possesses the path endowed with two types of contact, two types of feeling, two types of perception, two types of volition, two types of consciousness, two types of faith, two types of energy, two types of mindfulness, two types of concentration, and two types of wisdom?
One should not say so …pe… Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane virtue?
"Yes, [he does].
A possessor of the path possesses worldly contact, worldly feeling, worldly wisdom, worldly volition, worldly consciousness,
worldly faith, worldly energy, worldly mindfulness, and worldly concentration.
Is one who possesses mundane wisdom [likewise]?
One should not say so... [and so on]...
Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane virtue?
“Yes.
“Does one who possesses the path possess both mundane and supramundane contact …pe… and possess both mundane and supramundane wisdom?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane virtue? Yes.
Is one who possesses the path a worldling?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane right speech?
“Yes.
“Then one who possesses the path is endowed with mundane right view?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane right speech?
Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane right intention? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
Is he endowed with mundane right effort …pe… with mundane right mindfulness …pe… with mundane right concentration?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … that one who possesses the path is endowed with mundane right action … [as before] … mundane right livelihood?
"Yes.
"Does one who possesses the path possess mundane right view … pe … mundane right concentration?"
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right speech? Yes.
Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right view?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right speech? One should not say so.
“Yes.
“One who possesses the path [possesses] both mundane and supramundane right intention …pe… both mundane and supramundane right effort …pe…”
"Is he endowed with both mundane and supramundane right mindfulness...
[and] with both mundane and supramundane right concentration?
One should not say so... [and so on].
Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right action …pe… and right livelihood? Yes.
Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right view?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right livelihood? One should not say so.
“Yes.
“Then does one who possesses the path possess both mundane and supramundane right intention … pe … both mundane and supramundane right concentration?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “one who possesses the path is endowed with two kinds of virtue”?
“Yes.
“When mundane virtue has ceased, does the Path arise?
“Yes.”
“Does one who is immoral, whose virtue is broken, whose virtue is severed, develop the Path?
“One should not say so.
… [as before] … “Therefore, it follows that one who possesses the Path is endowed with two kinds of virtue.”
The Discussion on the Two Kinds of Virtue is finished.
